To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a Markovian Genetic Regulation Network can be controlled by an external variable; 2) the control algorithm can be implemented even in the imperfect information scenario; and 3) the performance of the imperfect information control algorithm is better than that of the perfect information one, in the sense that the imperfect information control strategy yields a lower performance index than the perfect information one for a given Markov Chain and a given performance index.

(a) we have developed an algorithm for the control of Markovian genetic networks in the imperfect information setting, (b) we have developed the corresponding control algorithm, (c) we have implemented our control algorithm, and (d) we have demonstrated the effectiveness of our control algorithm by applying it to a real-world genetic network, the p53 network.
